content.thinking: הכותרת "קרן השתלמות" מוכרת לי, ואני קורא את הטקסט: אפשר למשוך בלי מס אחרי שש שנים מההפקדה הראשונה, ולפני כן יש מס של לפחות 31%.
הפקדת המעסיק מגיעה רק אם אני חוסך בקרן, והרווחים פטורים ממס אחרי התקופה. מציע לי לבדוק אם מדד S&P 500 מתאים לי בתוך הקרן.

The savings chart shows the money is worth it even with an early withdrawal: 18,000 ₪ put in, 66,513 ₪ kept after tax. I'm now comparing the two funds' fees, where the 0.19% one comes out about 750 ₪ ahead.

Skipping the small text up top. Found "47%" next to an unclear Hebrew term ("מס") and will move on. Ignoring the "play with your numbers" fold since it doesn't apply, and noting that the "worth knowing" item asks when you can withdraw from the study fund tax-free after 6 years.
בדקתי את הטקסט הזה: הכסף זמין אחרי 6 שנים, והמשיכה לוקחת עד 4 ימי עסקים. השמות שמופיעים בו הם הראל, אלטשולר שחם ומיטב, ואני מכיר אותם מפרסומות.

The fees are up to 2% a year in management charges and no exit fee, and withdrawal after the waiting period is tax-exempt. An orange warning says early withdrawal is possible but costly, so I'm skipping the risks box since I don't know the term "בנאמנות".

content.text:
I'd keep it, definitely. It's a savings account that my boss pays into, and the page made it look like free money. I'm pretty sure about that. What sold me was the bar chart. On 300 ₪ a month from me and 900 from the employer, after 5 years I've put in "18,000 ₪", the employer adds "+54,000 ₪", and even after the "−13,974 ₪" tax for taking it out early I'm left with "66,513 ₪". As for when I can take it out: after "6 שנים" from the first deposit it's tax free. The page says it three times. Before that you can, but it's "יקרה", so don't touch it for 6 years. One thing to do: you can pick an S&P 500 track inside it, and I want to find out which company and track HR put me in.

How it went:
- **What I looked at, in order:**
  - The top heading and the "מה זה" part. That's where I got the 6 years, and also that taking it out early costs you, "לפחות 31%".
  - "למה משתמשים בזה". It says the employer's money only goes in here and the profits are tax free after the waiting time. Then the little buttons with track names, where I saw "מדד S&P 500".
  - The big bar chart, plus the fee line under it: 19 tracks, "66,280 ₪" at "0.7%" up to "67,028 ₪" at "0.19%". So cheap versus expensive is about 750 ₪ over 5 years, worth knowing.
  - "שווה לדעת" and "כסף נכנס ויוצא", which both say 6 years again. Money comes "עד 4 ימי עסקים" after you ask. I know the company names: הראל, אלטשולר שחם, מיטב.
  - "כמה זה עולה": "עד 2% בשנה" and "דמי יציאה — אין". 2% sounds small to me.
  - "מיסוי": tax free after the waiting time. An orange warning saying early withdrawal is expensive. I only read its first line.
- **Skipped:** the small text under the chart, the "שחקו עם המספרים שלכם" fold, most of "סיכונים ומה לא מוגן", and the table of terms at the bottom. I only glanced at that.
- **Where I wasn't sure:**
  - Somewhere there's "47%" next to "מס במקור". Is that 47% tax? I didn't understand it, and it scared me a bit.
  - The 31%, I'm not sure what it applies to.
  - The chart has 900 ₪ from the employer against 300 from me. Is mine really like that? No idea, it's not my numbers.
  - The chart has a red hatched bit before year 6. I guessed it means tax.
- **Words I didn't get:** "בנאמנות", "ותק", "הרווח הריאלי", "אג"ח ממשלתית צמודה", "הפקדה מוטבת", "מס במקור".
- **What bothered me:** the long part about taxes and the orange box was too much reading. I'd have stopped there, because I already had my answer by then.

input.answer: It's a savings account your employer pays into, and after 6 years from the first deposit you can take it out tax free. You can take it out earlier but you pay tax. Definitely worth having, the employer's money only comes this way (in the example I put in 18,000 and the employer added 54,000).
